title: Fountly
summary: A map of drinking water fountains worldwide. OpenStreetMap as the base; in Madrid, City Council data with the real status of each fountain. Built for personal use — and for anyone walking around thirsty.
problem: In Madrid at 38°C, not knowing where the nearest fountain is is a real problem. Searching «drinking fountain» in Maps doesn't always help, and the official data lives in a GeoJSON nobody opens on their phone.
audience: Me, friends and family. And anyone who walks and wants free water.
responsibilities: A world map that loads fountains on demand as you pan.
An OpenStreetMap (Overpass) adapter and, in Madrid, the City Council's official dataset.
Mobile UI: search, clustering, detail sheet and «Get directions».
decisions: OpenStreetMap as the global base; official datasets come in as verified exceptions with priority in their region.
Viewport loading and cell caching: don't fetch the same area twice when you come back.
Deliberately personal scope: useful for real before it becomes a product.
outcomes: Live at fountly.app, used on walks around Madrid.
In Madrid, the real status of each fountain: working, temporary or out of service.
